output.brief: The August dip comes from the failure of the east-riser chiller (CH-2) on 4 August, which left floors 6-8 at 26-29 C until it was fixed on 19 August. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and their overall score fell from 8.6 to 7.4. Scores for guests checking out 5-20 August were 6.8, and they recovered to 8.4 after the repair. Of the negative comments, 56 were about heat, and all 56 were from floors 6-8. Floors 1-5 were essentially flat. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates and kiosk metrics did not move, so I see no case against the housekeeping contractor or the kiosks. Do not serve notice on Orrin and do not pull the kiosks. Do not drop the floor 6-8 responses from the score, because that would hide a real problem. The next steps are to reinstate the deferred maintenance on both chillers, keep the critical spares on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Guests were already sent an apology and a goodwill credit, so a return-stay offer is optional. The value-for-money dip on floors 1-5 (8.0 to 7.7) is only slightly larger than the usual August dip, so the 6% rate rise may have played a small part. Watch value scores in September rather than reversing the rate rise now. I am fairly confident in this and collected no further evidence.
output.methodChoice: Applied the diagnostic sequence to the initial evidence only and collected no catalogue items. The evidence already separates the floor blocks and the dates clearly.
